arbaeen_ahadith.front: Who narrates the ḥadīth on innovation (Arbaʿīn 5)?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: ʿĀʾishah RA, the Mother of the Believers

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What kunya did the Prophet ﷺ give ʿĀʾishah RA, and after whom?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Umm ʿAbd Allāh — <bdi>أُمُّ عَبْدِ اللهِ</bdi> — after her nephew, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Where did the Prophet ﷺ marry ʿĀʾishah RA, and when did she move in with him?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: He married her in Makkah; she moved in with him in the second year after the Hijrah

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How old was ʿĀʾishah RA when the Prophet ﷺ died?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Only 18

arbaeen_ahadith.front: When did ʿĀʾishah RA die, and who led her funeral prayer?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: In 57 AH, more than forty years after the Prophet ﷺ — Abū Hurayrah RA led her janāzah

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What standing in knowledge did ʿĀʾishah RA have among the Companions?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: She was one of the most knowledgeable of them — senior Companions came to her with their questions

arbaeen_ahadith.text: {{c1::2,210}} aḥādīth are narrated from ʿĀʾishah RA, {{c2::174}} of them muttafaq ʿalayh

arbaeen_ahadith.front: In the ḥadīth on innovation (Arbaʿīn 5), what becomes of whatever someone introduces into “this matter of ours” that is not from it?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: It is rejected — <bdi>فَهُوَ رَدٌّ</bdi> (Bukhārī and Muslim)

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does Muslim's second wording of the ḥadīth on innovation say, and why is it the wider of the two?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: “Whoever does an act that our matter is not upon, it is rejected.” It covers anyone who does such an act, not only the one who first introduced it.

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Imām Aḥmad held that Islam is built on three ḥadīth: {{c1::“Actions are only by intentions”}} (Arbaʿīn 1); {{c2::“Whoever introduces into this matter of ours…”}} (Arbaʿīn 5); and {{c3::“The permissible is clear…”}} (Arbaʿīn 6)
arbaeen_ahadith.extra: So the ḥadīth on innovation explains one of Islam's foundational teachings.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is the ḥadīth on innovation the scale for, and how does it pair with the ḥadīth on intentions?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Outward acts. A deed not upon the Sharīʿah's guidance is rejected, just as a deed that isn't sincere is rejected — so once we are sincere, the outward performance must also be correct.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Among which kind of the Prophet's ﷺ sayings is the ḥadīth on innovation counted?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: <bdi>جَوَامِع الكَلِم</bdi> — the concise, comprehensive sayings he was given: few words, profound meaning

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What kind of “new” thing is the ḥadīth on innovation about?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: A new theological belief or a new ritual devotional practice — it clarifies the concept, and the consequence, of adding one

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is <bdi>بِدْعَة</bdi> linguistically?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Something new — newly invented

arbaeen_ahadith.text: In the Sharīʿah, a <bdi>بِدْعَة</bdi> is a religious innovation: {{c1::not done — in word or deed, explicitly or implicitly — in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, the rightly guided caliphs or the early generations}}, {{c2::though the need for it existed then}}; {{c3::with no proof for it in the Qurʾān, the Sunnah or ijmāʿ}}; and done {{c4::to gain more reward}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What two things make an innovation blameworthy?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: It has no proof, evidence or basis in the Sharīʿah — and the person believes it is part of the dīn

arbaeen_ahadith.front: In the lesson on the ḥadīth on innovation, what is Islam, as opposed to innovating?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Submission and following

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Between Islam and people, which way does the ḥadīth on innovation make sure the change runs?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Islam changes the people — not the other way round

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does Allah command in the verse cited with the ḥadīth on innovation?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: “This is My path, leading straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways” — al-Anʿām 6:153

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Which innovations are rejected, and where above all?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Every blameworthy innovation — above all in acts of worship

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What new things do not go against the teachings of the Sharīʿah?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Compiling the Qurʾān and the ḥadīth, codifying the Islamic sciences, and the like

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Imām al-Shāfiʿī: what has been innovated that goes against {{c1::the Qurʾān, the Sunnah, consensus or a narration}} is {{c2::a misguided innovation}}; whatever has been invented that goes against none of these is {{c3::a praiseworthy innovation}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Which of ʿUmar RA's acts shows the word bidʿah used in its linguistic sense?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Gathering the people for tarāwīḥ behind one imām, of which he said “What an excellent bidʿah this is” — <bdi>نِعْمَتِ البِدْعَةُ هَذِهِ</bdi>

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does the lesson on the ḥadīth on innovation conclude about Islam itself?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: That it is a perfect and complete religion, which doesn't need to be altered, changed or reformed

vocab.meaning: to introduce something new, to originate (literally, to bring forth) — in fiqh, to break one's wuḍūʾ
vocab.source: Arbaʿīn, Ḥadīth 5 — vocab in the class notes, 2026-10-14

vocab.extra: to introduce something new · Form IV · <bdi>مَنْ أَحْدَثَ فِي أَمْرِنَا هَذَا مَا لَيْسَ مِنْهُ فَهُوَ رَدٌّ</bdi> (Arbaʿīn 5) · same root as <bdi>الحَدَث</bdi>, ritual impurity
